title: Street Sports Basketball
build: XPB disk, Scratch of Triangle directory
uncounted: loaded with the game, excluded by default as screen RAM

the RAM under the I/O area holds data, and game.json does not say what it is (kit/skills/c64/c64-reference, "RAM the CPU cannot see"); $D400-$D5FE is copied there after the hand-over, which holds it at $0200
loaded with the game, after selection_rle_fbe8 ($FBE8)

records.c: Sets up the 6510 port and stack, initializes the KERNAL and VIC, installs the menu's two IRQ entries and common NMI return, then initializes the RAM music driver and draws the opening screen.
Selects RAM under the KERNAL with port value $25, calls the music entry at $E003, and restores $26 before drawing the opening screen.
Starts a 1000-tick wait at $08F9-$08FA. Drains pending GETIN characters and then waits for a new key, either joystick's active-low fire bit, or the IRQ counter to reach zero.
Clears VIC screen enable and jumps into the selection setup at $1288.
RTI target installed in both the KERNAL NMI vector and the hardware NMI vector.
Decrements the opening-screen counter if it is nonzero, banks in the RAM music driver for one tick, restores the KERNAL and continues its normal IRQ at $EA31.
Low byte of the timer initialized to $03E8 on the opening screen.
High byte of the opening timer. The IRQ decrements it when the low byte rolls over.
Saves A, X, Y and the processor port, calls the same music tick with RAM visible at $E000, acknowledges CIA1, restores registers and returns from the interrupt directly.
67 glyphs of eight bitmap bytes each. The menu uses screen-code indices for letters, digits and spaces, and index $40 for the name-entry cursor.
Selects VIC bank $4000 via CIA2, sets the VIC memory pointers and enables multicolour bitmap mode with a grey background and black border.
Resets the port permissions and the two option-strip positions. Copies 14-byte default names into $0370 and $037E unless the menu restart flag is set.
Ten little-endian pointers to the draft biographies, in the same order as the character choices.
Little-endian pointers to the instruction panels for court, opponent, difficulty, side, naming, coin flip, draft and start.
Four page-high bytes for the School, Alley, Suburbs and City preview records. The menu combines each with a zero low byte.
Two page-high bytes for the human and computer opponent pictures.
Four page-high bytes used for coin faces and related pictures. The first two are the heads and tails panels.
Ten page-high bytes corresponding to the ten draft portraits at $2000-$47E1.
Default green-team field copied into menu workspace, padded to 13 cells and terminated by $FF.
Default blue-team field copied into menu workspace, padded to 13 cells and terminated by $FF.
Reads four pages from RAM under $D800-$DBFF and writes them to colour RAM at the same CPU addresses, switching the 6510 port on each read and write.

Expands value and repeat-count pairs from RAM at $EFE8 into the bitmap starting at $6B40. Copies the $EC00-$EFFF screen-colour pages to $5C00 and banks between RAM at $DC00 and colour RAM to restore the second colour plane.
Returns the address $6000 + 320 times $0338 + eight times $0339 in $033A-$033B. Preserves A, X, Y and the two temporary pointer bytes on the stack.
Computes $091E + eight times the character index in A. Copies eight bytes to the bitmap destination in $033A-$033B with $55 ORed into each byte.
Fetches the same eight-byte glyph as the regular draw routine, inverts the bits, ORs in $55 and writes the result to the bitmap destination.
Ignores $FF. For other codes it computes the current bitmap cell address and calls the regular glyph writer.
Skips $FF and $42. For other codes it computes the current bitmap cell address and calls the inverted glyph writer.

Clears the KERNAL key buffer and reads GETIN while updating a team-name field. It also polls for joystick confirmation before editing. RETURN accepts, DEL backs up and redraws the cursor, and the accepted name ends in $FF.

Draws an option strip from the pointer in X:Y, finds the first word and highlights it. Polls the two sticks, moves the highlight and updates the preview on left or right, then returns the firing port in X.
Scans the option line forward from the current selection, skipping separators. Updates the selection index and cursor field for the next highlight.
Scans backward for the preceding selectable word and updates the option index and field position.
Polls port 1 first, then port 2 if port 1 reports no horizontal direction or fire. Records which port reacted in $0399.
Unless $03A0 disables this side, decodes active-low direction bits from CIA1 port B into X and Y deltas and returns active-low fire in carry.
Unless $03A1 disables this side, decodes active-low direction bits from CIA1 port A into X and Y deltas and returns active-low fire in carry.
Resets $03A2 and calls the selection setup, then blanks the picture and hands the name and length of SORTER to the disk transition.
Six-byte PETSCII filename passed to the transition routine at $1D40.
Length supplied in A beside the SORTER string pointer.

Reads width, height and an origin from an image record in X:Y. Carry substitutes the current cursor origin. Each cell consumes eight bitmap bytes and a pair of colour bytes, and the source banking is chosen by $039F.
Calculates a 40-column cell index from the cursor row and column for the two colour planes.
Prompt strip for School, Alley, Suburbs and City, terminated by $FF.
Screen-code labels for the two opponent modes.
Menu strip containing the Easy, Intermediate and Tough labels.
Heads and Tails labels for the coin flip.
Button-to-continue prompt. Code $41 supplies the internal word separator drawn as a blank glyph.
Button-when-ready prompt, also using $41 within the phrase.
Play Game and Start Over option labels with two-word choices joined by $41.
Working strip with ten character slots in the draft. The prep code copies its default from $1515.
Template copied to $14FC before either team makes a pick. The $42 bytes mark positions of the ten selectable figures.

Redraws the backdrop and resets the menu fields, then uses the prompt table and horizontal picker for court, opponent, and difficulty when a computer is selected. Continues through names, coin choice and the draft.
Small indexed table used at $1613 to translate the difficulty selection before storing it in $0396.
Displays the side-selection prompt and assigns green to whichever port supplies fire. The later naming code uses that assignment to select which joystick can confirm each name.
Displays the green name and editing instructions, positions the text cursor, and opens the name editor with the green-team buffer at $0370.
Picks the name prompt and its default field for the remaining naming phase, updates which joystick the editor accepts and calls the same editor.
Chooses the one- or two-player coin prompt using $0393, draws the heads/tails options, and stores the choice and calling side at $1428-$142A.
Displays the coin-flipping panel, runs the timed sprite sequence, then draws the chosen outcome panel and announces which team gets first pick.
Draws the two explanatory panels from the prompt table, putting a fire-to-continue strip beneath each one before entering the draft code at $18C0.
Runs the draft and offers Play Game or Start Over. Start Over jumps back into the menu at $1533 with the restart flag set.
Ten little-endian pointers to cells in $A000-$ACA7. The selection redraw places these pictures using their built-in starting columns.
Ten little-endian pointers to the separate player views at $B000-$BB17. The redraw can substitute roster positions for their built-in origin.
Initializes the roster and pick order, then repeats the selection round. The enabled port and on-screen turn name follow the team whose pick is due.
Converts the highlighted slot through the current availability array, marks the original character as used, and redraws the spot and roster using their separate picture records.
Return from the draft selection routine.
A full blank menu line with a terminator, used to clear the status area.
Phrase appended to the team name when the heads choice is shown.
Phrase appended for the tails choice.
Phrase appended to the winning side's name.
Prefix printed before the name of the team whose draft turn is next.
Wait message shown while the computer chooses a roster member.
Dispatches on the preview mode at $142B. Draws a court, opponent, portrait or coin panel. During the draft it also updates the biography and positions the three-layer cursor using $1969.
Converts the highlighted slot through $191D to a character number and selects its text via the pointer table at $0C1C.
Masks interrupts, selects bank value $25 and jumps into the transition entry in RAM at $FF83.
Clears the picked flags and both three-player rosters, restores selection positions, determines which port is enabled for first pick, and enables the three selection sprites.
Clears the first two pointer sprite slots and writes their visible raster rows in three-byte groups.

Starts at the frame attribute table at $5B00 and coordinates at $4E00. Advances by 16 attribute bytes and 32 coordinate bytes per frame, passing each sprite to VIC registers and writing pointers in $5FF8-$5FFF.
Preserves X and runs a nested delay loop. Called each animation frame and between coin panels.

Sixteen 32-byte coordinate records used by the coin sprite player. Indexed loads pick each sprite's coordinate pair and add X and Y placement constants.
Global colour sent to VIC sprite multicolour register 1 before the coin animation.
Global colour sent to VIC sprite multicolour register 0 before the coin animation.
Number of coin animation frames, 16. The frame loop compares its index against this byte.
The first 16 sprite shape slots in the animation bank. The frame player converts shape indices in the attribute table using VIC pointer offset $44.
Sprite shape slots 16 through 31. The coordinate and attribute tables choose combinations of these shapes to assemble moving coin frames.
Final eight sprite shape slots selected by the coin animation's attribute records.
Sixteen frames of eight sprite pairs. Each pair holds a shape number and a flag/colour byte. The low nibble sets the individual colour and high bits select multicolour and expansion.
Title screen colour matrix. The two nibbles in each of the 1000 cells provide colours for the multicolour bitmap at $6000.
Second title colour page, beginning at cell 256. The VIC uses both nibbles as bitmap colours for the logo area.
Third title colour page, beginning at cell 512 and covering most of the large outlined lettering.
Final visible portion of the title colour matrix, including the copyright row.
Title bitmap rows 0 to 2, including the Epyx logo above the main title. Every row holds 320 bytes.

Four pages of RAM hidden under colour RAM. At startup the routine at $0C86 reads these bytes with I/O hidden and copies them to the visible colour plane.
Four pages hidden under I/O. The selection backdrop routine at $0D13 transfers them to colour RAM below the screen's multicolour bitmap.
Entry shared by both menu IRQ routines. Jumps into the player at $E0BC for one music update.
Resets the sound player at $E073, then selects tune 1 through $E02F.
Initializes the driver and runs it at a raster boundary, instead of using an IRQ. The countdown changes to tune 2 on falling through.
Low byte of the countdown decremented by the raster-timed music entry.
High byte of the countdown for the change to tune 2.
Uses the tune number in A to index a four-byte entry at $E495. For each enabled voice with sufficient priority, puts its stream pointer in zero page and resets its event countdown.
Builds eight octaves of frequency words at $FE00 by shifting the 12 base words at $E474. Clears SID registers and the player's zero-page workspace.

Services each enabled voice, handling its countdown or fetching an event. The byte dispatcher stops the stream at $FF, sends note bytes to $E3CC and sends commands at $C0 and above through the pointer table at $E43A.
Oscillates pulse width between the driver's bounds and writes the new width to each voice selected by the mask at $3C.
Periodically reverses the pitch step of each voice in the mask at $42, updates its frequency word and writes the result to the SID.
Offsets 0, 7 and 14 from the first SID voice register block.
Reads two bytes and writes them verbatim to the active voice's frequency registers.
Reads one byte into the active voice's control shadow and writes it to the SID.
Reads two operand bytes directly into the active voice's pulse-width registers.
Reads the two operands for attack/decay and sustain/release.
Reads the low and high cutoff bytes, retaining the high byte in $39.
Subtracts one operand from the cached cutoff high byte, stores it to the SID and reads a duration.
Adds to the cached high cutoff byte and uses the same store and duration path.
Sets the upper four routing/resonance bits and combines them with the stored enabled input mask.
Adds an operand to the volume shadow and keeps the low nibble before updating the SID.
Sets the low volume nibble and preserves the stored filter-mode bits.
Stores one operand directly to the current voice countdown and ends processing for the voice for this tick.
Sets the current voice bit in the filter input mask and updates the routing register.
Keeps the upper operand bits for the filter mode and combines them with the current volume.
Clears one voice's bit in the filter input mask and updates the SID routing register.
Copies one argument into the per-voice byte indexed at $27. The stream control flow continues with the next event.
Reads a little-endian address and replaces the active voice's stream pointer.
Stores the operand in the current voice's repeat counter at $24 plus the voice number.
Reads a target address, decrements the repeat counter and jumps there while the counter stays nonzero.
Subtracts an operand from the high frequency byte before the common register write and duration read.
Subtracts an operand from the low frequency byte and propagates borrow to the high byte.
Adds an operand to the high frequency byte before the common write and duration read.
Adds an operand to the low frequency byte and propagates carry to the high byte.
Reads the step and period into the active voice's modulation fields and sets its enable bit in $42.
Clears the selected voice's bit in $42.
Sets the selected voice's bit in the pulse sweep mask at $3C.
Clears the selected voice's bit in that sweep mask.
One bit per voice used to test or set modulation enables.
Complements of the voice-enable bits, used to clear the selected bit.
Stores a one-byte offset for the voice and sets its enable marker at $41.
Clears the voice's frequency-offset enable bit.
Derives a frequency index from the SID oscillator readout and jumps to the note-frequency writer.
Note $60 clears the gate. Other note values index frequency words at $FE00 and open the gate after any enabled offset. Reads a duration byte whose high bit controls the timed gate release.
Reads the next byte through the selected zero-page voice pointer and increments that pointer with carry into its high byte.
Twenty-nine little-endian handler addresses for stream commands $C0-$DC.
Twelve starting frequency words. Initialization repeatedly shifts them down to build the other octave entries.
Byte-offset table used to arrange the 12-note octave bands in the generated frequency table.
Two four-byte tune assignments, each with three stream IDs and a priority byte.
Four stream entry addresses. Tune 1 selects three different streams and tune 2 selects the volume sequence.
Effect stream assigned to all voices by tune 2. Steps the volume down from fifteen and uses rest events between the changes.
98 note/rest events and 94 envelope commands, with repeat counters and jumps. The stream ends at $E6BC.
58 note/rest events with repeats and pitch modulation commands. The stream ends at $E754.
Beginning of the third opening voice, with an envelope, waveform, pulse-width and modulation changes interleaved with note events.
Tail of the third opening voice. Stream terminator is $FF at $EB69.
First 256 bytes of the selection screen matrix restored to $5C00 by $0CE6.
Second 256 bytes of the selection screen matrix restored to $5D00.
Third 256 bytes of the selection screen matrix restored to $5E00.
Last 232 visible cells of the selection screen matrix restored to $5F00.
512 selection bitmap value/count pairs expand to $6B40-$6FD9 through the loop at $0CBC.
512 selection bitmap value/count pairs expand to $6FDA-$7397 through the loop at $0CBC.
512 selection bitmap value/count pairs expand to $7398-$7B01 through the loop at $0CBC.
154 selection bitmap value/count pairs expand to $7B02-$7F3F through the loop at $0CBC.
Calls the common disk overlay routine and enters the menu from $0800.
Calls the common disk overlay routine, silences the SID and disables VIC and CIA1 interrupts, then jumps to the match entry at $0E03.
Hides the I/O area and swaps seven pages at $0800-$0EFF and $D000-$D6FF byte for byte. Returns with I/O visible and the KERNAL hidden.
